A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KaVa research, with matching methods and identifiable retained experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. A table overlap in v2 is recoverable through text extraction.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and the appendices report original benchmark results, efficiency measurements, ablations, decoded latent traces and KV-cache analyses, alongside attributed baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds MetaMathQA experiments, training-data-size ablations and evaluations using alternative teacher-generated traces.

M1.justification: v1's student replaces the entire reasoning trace with latent tokens. v2 additionally introduces hybrid reasoning, retaining explicit tokens before or after the latent sequence and incorporating them into the student loss (Section 4.1; Appendix G). This substantially extends training and inference behavior, although the underlying KV-cache compression and matching mechanism remains unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 trains on GSM8k-Aug and GSM8k-Aug-NL and evaluates GSM8k, GSM8k-Hard and SVAMP. v2 adds MetaMathQA training, including MATH-derived problems and longer traces, plus MATH500, multiArith and DeepMind-Mathematics evaluation. This broadens the represented mathematical problems beyond the original arithmetic coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 fills previously missing Llama-1B comparisons: PCCoT appears on GSM8k-Hard and SVAMP under both training datasets, and CODI appears on those benchmarks after GSM8k-Aug-NL training. The baseline families otherwise remain unchanged; Table 2's grouped method labels primarily reflect shared inference behavior.

E3.justification: New MetaMathQA experiments vary replacement ratios and latent placement, use five epochs and batch size 64, and disable KaVa's CODI loss. Only non-diverged CODI/PCCoT runs are reported. Appendix H adds dataset-fraction and training-budget controls; Appendix I adds trace-generation and filtering protocols. The original GSM8k settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of hybrid replacement ratio and placement, training-data quantity versus matched training steps, and alternative trace generators (Appendices G–I). Existing component, loss, eviction and iteration ablations, decoded examples and cache-similarity analyses are retained. Appendix F primarily redisplays benchmark results rather than introducing a separate robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions already specify three seeds and standard-error reporting. v2 extends uncertainty reporting to Llama-1B CODI comparisons previously represented by cited point estimates, such as 53.9 ± 0.5 on GSM8k after GSM8k-Aug training. No explicit increase in run counts is stated; changing parentheses to ± alone is cosmetic.

E6.justification: v2 adds MetaMathQA and data-sensitivity outcomes and revises several Llama-1B baseline results. For GSM8k-Aug training and GSM8k testing, Full CoT accuracy changes from 61.6 to 63.4 and forward passes from 65 to 31.9. KaVa remains at 56.5 accuracy and 6.9 passes, changing its reported reduction from 89% to 78%. These are baseline revisions, not improved KaVa scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the formal cache definitions and Appendix A's eviction pseudocode retain their mathematical content. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about compressed-cache self-distillation, natural-language robustness, scaling and efficiency. The revised second contribution emphasizes existing compressors and direct cache generation, both already described in v1, without substantively changing the overall claim scope.

C2.justification: Appendix G introduces explanations for weak fully latent MetaMathQA performance, including limited latent capacity and fewer unique training questions, and discusses instability and hybrid reasoning as a remedy. Appendices H–I interpret data dependence and trace-length/source effects. Section 7 adds interpretability qualifications and a speculative safety argument about distilled reasoners.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C add MetaMathQA's dataset identifier, size, trace length and hyperparameter column. Appendix I documents prompting, generation modes, answer filtering, retries, fallback to GPT-4 traces and deduplication. These substantially extend reproducibility information for the new experiments; existing pseudocode and GSM8k hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds System1.5 and clarifies the use of existing cache-compression methods. Additional citations support the new datasets, teacher models and safety discussion. The principal positioning against CODI, PCCoT and KV-Distill remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized contribution and related-work edits, added experimental explanations, an ethics/reproducibility section, new appendix sections and the publication header. The existing narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds multi-panel MetaMathQA, accuracy-efficiency, data-size and teacher-trace displays; expands dataset and hyperparameter tables; and regroups Table 2. Existing key/value heatmaps exchange main-text and appendix placement without new underlying analyses. A layout regression causes Figures 5–6 to obscure part of Table 3's last row.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical support for scalability through longer-trace mathematics evaluations, hybrid reasoning experiments and controlled studies of data quantity and supervision source. These additions reveal failure conditions as well as strengths, while filling missing baseline comparisons. Some Figure 14 points retain older baseline values inconsistent with Tables 1–2, Table 3 suffers overlap, and MetaMathQA comparisons exclude diverged baseline runs. These limitations reduce clarity and comparison strength but do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and understanding.
